problem:
Which of the following sets are orthonormal?

- $U={[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}]}$
- $V={[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 9\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}28 \\ -21 \\ -7\end{aligned}]}$
- $W={[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{5} \\ \frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{5} \\ -\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]}$

feedback.problem:
Which of the following sets are orthonormal?

- $U={[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}]}$
- $V={[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -1 \\ -7\end{aligned}]}$
- $W={[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]}$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of the given sets as 
${{u}_{1},{u}_{2}},$ 
${{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}},$ and 
${{w}_{1},{w}_{2}},$ respectively. 

The sets $U,V,$ and $W$ are orthonormal if the following conditions on each set hold:

- ${u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{2}=0\,\text{and}\,{\begin{aligned}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}=1 \\ {u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}=1.\end{aligned}$

- ${\begin{aligned}{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{2}=0 \\ {v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{3}=0 \\ {v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{3}=0\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,{\begin{aligned}{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}=1 \\ {v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}=1 \\ {v}_{3}\cdot {v}_{3}=1.\end{aligned}$

- ${w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{2}=0\,\text{and}\,{\begin{aligned}{w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{1}=1 \\ {w}_{2}\cdot {w}_{2}=1.\end{aligned}$

With that in mind, let's examine our sets in turn.

- For the set $U,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}]=-\frac{6}{13}+\frac{6}{13}=0 & ✓ \\ {u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}]=\frac{4}{13}+\frac{9}{13}=1 & ✓ \\ {u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}]=\frac{9}{13}+\frac{4}{13}=1 & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, the set $U$ is orthonormal.

- For the set $V,$ notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -4\end{aligned}]=0+1+8=9\ne 0 & \times \end{aligned}
$$

So, $V$ is not an orthonormal set.

- For the set $W,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]=\frac{2}{5}-\frac{2}{5}=0 & ✓ \\ {w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]=\frac{4}{5}+\frac{1}{5}=1 & ✓ \\ {w}_{2}\cdot {w}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]=\frac{1}{5}+\frac{4}{5}=1 & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, $W$ is an orthonormal set.

Therefore, we conclude that the correct answer is "$U$ and $W$ only".
